claims.claim: Civilizations die and recovery requires a specific pattern that is recursive and testable.
claims.plain_english: The way civilizations fall apart and how they can recover follows a repeating pattern that can be checked and proven.
claims.evidence_given: The document states the pattern is recursive and testable but provides no specific evidence or examples in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a civilization could die without following this pattern, or if recovery could happen without the described sequence, the claim would be false.

claims.claim: The synchronization problem is the load-bearing structure of the Nucleation Thesis.
claims.plain_english: The synchronization problem is the most important idea that holds the whole theory together.
claims.evidence_given: The document names the synchronization problem as the load-bearing structure before asking the reader to follow the full derivation.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the synchronization problem could be removed without collapsing the thesis, or if another problem were more central, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: The pattern of civilizational death and recovery is recursive.
claims.plain_english: The same pattern repeats itself over and over again in different civilizations.
claims.evidence_given: The document repeats that the pattern is recursive but offers no historical examples or data in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If a civilization died or recovered in a way that did not fit the pattern, or if the pattern only applied to one civilization, the claim would be false.

claims.claim: The pattern of civilizational death and recovery is testable.
claims.plain_english: You can check whether the pattern is true by looking at real civilizations.
claims.evidence_given: The document asserts testability but provides no methodology, criteria, or examples in this interlude.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the pattern could not be checked against real historical data, or if any test would be impossible to perform, the claim would be false.

claims.claim: The full canonical treatment of the Nucleation Thesis contains the complete argument, tables, proofs, and source structure.
claims.plain_english: The main version of the thesis has all the detailed evidence, charts, and references.
claims.evidence_given: The document links to a canonical page and states it contains the complete argument, tables, proofs, and source structure.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the linked canonical page did not contain tables, proofs, or source structure, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: The interlude sends the reader to the canonical page instead of replacing it.
claims.plain_english: This short version points you to the full version rather than trying to be the full version itself.
claims.evidence_given: The document explicitly states this in multiple places and provides a link to the canonical page.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the interlude actually contained the full argument and replaced the canonical page, this claim would be false.

claims.claim: The sequence of the Nucleation Thesis is: The Thread, The Synchronization Problem, The Sequence, Five Vectors One Cascade.
claims.plain_english: The thesis is organized into four main steps in a specific order.
claims.evidence_given: The document presents a timeline with these four nodes and their descriptions.
claims.what_would_break_it: If the actual thesis had a different structure or order, this claim would be false.
